messages:
kevin_sales: Heads-up — customer (AcmePayments) reported a sudden drop in quality after an automatic regional failover at ~2026-03-15T11:14Z. They say responses are truncated and contain strange token fragments. Request id: req_0a1b2c. Can support triage?

ash_support: Got it. Can you paste a minimal repro prompt + the full request id + the timestamp they provided? Also which model they were calling originally?

kevin_sales: From customer: 'Prompt: Summarize invoice #INV-9987' — they claim they were pinned to `open-7b-v2` in us-east-1 but logs show a failover to eu-west and the model in response metadata is `open-7b-lite-q4`. Sample request id above. Timestamp in their logs: 2026-03-15T11:14:22Z.

ash_support: Thanks. @deploy-bot can you drop the routing events around that req id?

deploy-bot: [11:14:21Z] route_decision: req=req_0a1b2c region_hint=us-east-1 -> selected_region=eu-west-1 reason=capacity_surge fallback_variant=open-7b-lite-q4 fallback_policy=allow_any_variant

ash_support: Repro steps requested from customer — asked them to rerun with debug headers. Meanwhile can someone from eng check variant compatibility?

jin_eng: Looking. Quick hypothesis: the lite variant uses a different tokenizer/vocab build (q4 quantized runtime) which can produce different spacing and OOV tokenization for some unicode/ligature sequences — that explains the 'weird token fragments'. It's not a generation bug, it's mismatch of tokenizer semantics.

kevin_sales: Customer is upset because their downstream parsing pipeline expects token boundaries from the full model. Billing worry: they saw a spike in tokens billed because the lite variant emits more tokens for the same input.

ash_support: Asking customer to attach the raw response they received. Also suggested temp mitigation: set `X-Region: eu-west-1` header OR pin `variant=open-7b-v2` if their plan allows.

customer_ops: We reproduced locally following this:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-Region: us-east-1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-7b-v2","prompt":"Summarize invoice #INV-9987","max_tokens":64}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They saw metadata: `served_variant: open-7b-lite-q4` and body contains tokens like `@@--ĠInv` (broken fragments).

jin_eng: Can you also paste the `model_metadata` from the response? Need tokenizer_version and merges_hash.

customer_ops: From response: `tokenizer_version: v2.1`, `merges_hash: 9a7f3c`. From customer config/service before failover they showed `tokenizer_version: v2.4`, `merges_hash: d2b1e0` (for open-7b-v2).

jin_eng: That confirms it. Different tokenizer versions -> token id mapping changes -> different token counts and boundary splits. Two-pronged mitigation: 1) Short-term: set customer's routing policy to disallow variants with incompatible tokenizers (change fallback_policy to compatible-only for their tenant). 2) Medium-term: enforce tokenizer compatibility at runtime (reject failovers to variants with different tokenizer metadata) and add a conversion step if we must fall back.

rachel_sre: We can immediately update the tenant route for AcmePayments to prefer pinned variant and avoid cross-region failover for them. Will need a deploy window? This is a config change that can be applied to routing service without code.

olga_prodops: FYI this was triggered by a us-east-1 spike at 11:14Z. We have standby capacity in eu-west but it contains some quantized/lite variants to save cost — that is why fallback selected the lite variant. We should add a note in runbook to avoid mixing tokenizer families across regional standby pools.

ash_support: Action items:
- @rachel_sre apply tenant routing override for AcmePayments to prefer `open-7b-v2` and set fallback_policy=compatible-only.
- @jin_eng add a validator to the route decision service to compare tokenizer metadata before selecting a fallback variant (short PR).
- @olga_prodops schedule a config sync to ensure standby pools have a compatible tokenizer set.
- Support to send customer a mitigation guide (pinning, headers, temporary credits if billed extra).

kevin_sales: Customer asks for ETA — can we provide an ETA for the routing override?

rachel_sre: I can push the routing override in ~30 minutes, will confirm when complete (INC-20260315-847).

jin_eng: I'll open a trunk PR for the validator and aim for a 2-day turnaround. If urgent we can hotfix route decision to add a tokenizer-compat check as a quick gate.

ash_support: I told the customer we'll apply a routing override within 30-60m and follow up with eng plan. Also offered a one-off credit for the token delta (billing flagged).

customer_ops: Confirmed they'll wait for the override and will provide one more sample if issue persists. Thanks.

kevin_sales: Thanks everyone. Please post updates here after routing override + PR created.

rachel_sre: Routing override applied at 11:41Z. Verified subsequent requests for req ids after 11:41Z show `served_variant=open-7b-v2` for that tenant.

jin_eng: PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4312 — adds tokenizer metadata check to route_decision.

ash_support: Customer notified and accepted credit offer. Marking as monitoring for 24h.

kevin_sales: Closing loop — customer happy for now, will reopen if anything else crops up.
